company.name: ABC Roofing & Remodeling
company.operatingModel: Multi-branch residential roofing/remodeling contractor with centralized governance and branch operations.

publicConstraints: Multi-office Florida roofing operations exist across Tampa, Orlando and Jacksonville.
Industry growth example supports hundreds of annual sold roof replacements at high-volume scale.
Typical lead-to-final-invoice cycle commonly spans roughly two weeks to one month.
Quote acceptance to job start commonly falls within roughly one to three weeks.
evidenceBoundary.syntheticClientData: All ABC volumes, customers, employees, dates, financials, issues, capacities and performance are fictional but internally reconciled.
evidenceBoundary.governanceDerived: Flags, readiness states, carryover and management queues must be calculated from supplied synthetic records rather than manually asserted.

annualModel.rationale: Modeled as a mature ~200-person three-branch contractor at a scale comparable to publicly described high-volume roofing operations; values are synthetic, not attributed to a real company.

september.purpose: Closed operating month and governance checkpoint.
september.law: Every September headline count must reconcile to identifiable job/event records.

october.law: Scheduled jobs must be identifiable carryover/current jobs with scheduling evidence. Forecast intake/capacity must be labeled modeled and remain distinct from committed scheduled work.

reconciliationLaw: No dashboard metric may exist independently of the underlying synthetic jobs/events from which it is calculated.
